clue.text: Rubbish dumps

definitions.meaning: to rubbish an idea is to dismiss it scornfully, a verb sense
nursery slang for droppings or faeces, taken as a mass noun, so the plural clue word matches

explanation.surface: Rubbish tips, described in two words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish dumps' reads as one phrase about landfill sites; it is two separate definitions, the verb 'rubbish' and the childish word for what one dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully is the verb sense; the reduplicated nursery word for excrement is the noun sense.

clue.text: Choose wrapping to match up with East German toy

indicators.note: the word for choose is wrapped around the next pieces

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for match is read upwards

parts.note: colours that go together match
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: Picking out a toy from the old GDR.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match up' looks like pairing off, but in a down answer 'up' turns the word for match, and German supplies the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogo stick is a spring-loaded stick for bouncing on, a children's plaything.

clue.text: Port boundaries to lure in huge birds

indicators.note: the port and boundaries go in the letters for huge

parts.note: OS, outsize, is a clothing abbreviation meaning very large
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Harbour limits attract huge birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge' looks like an adjective for the birds but is the clothing size; 'in' puts the port and the ends of 'lure' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orioles are brightly coloured songbirds.

clue.text: A good part for a communicator?

indicators.note: part means divide, so the word for for is split by the other pieces

parts.note: per means for, as in a pound per head

explanation.surface: A good role for someone who talks to people?
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a noun (a role) but is a verb: PER parts to take A G.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a device that receives messages, so it serves as a communicator.

clue.text: Filthy rich — a logical description of such government?

definitions.text: Filthy rich — a logical description of such government?

indicators.note: filthy suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rule by the obscenely wealthy is logically described thus.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of RICH A LOGICAL gives the answer, and the whole clue describes rule by a rich few.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is government by a small elite, often the very wealthy.

clue.text: Britain allows monarch to be a Muslim

indicators.note: allows means lets in, so the abbreviation for Britain takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch
the infinitive phrase is the verb be

explanation.surface: Britain lets the monarch become a follower of Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are a North African people, overwhelmingly followers of Islam, so one is an example of a Muslim.

clue.text: Thought-provoking musical man recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the musical and the man are read in reverse

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
cove is old British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A musical about a man, remembered as stimulating.
explanation.walkthrough: EVITACOVE read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative brings memories and images to mind, stirring thought.

clue.text: Enter into Christianity, point being to enter the cloth

indicators.note: the point is to go into the word for cloth

parts.note: baize is the green cloth on snooker and card tables

explanation.surface: A churchy notion: joining the faith means joining the clergy, 'the cloth'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' suggests the clergy, but it is BAIZE, with PT inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is the rite of admission into the Christian church.

clue.text: An Italian woman, as Mr Ross would say

indicators.note: Jonathan Ross, the British TV presenter, pronounces his Rs as Ws

parts.note: the clue word as spoken by that presenter

explanation.surface: An Italian lady, in the voice of a chat-show host.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross, a British chat-show host, famously says W for R, so the answer in his mouth comes out as 'woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rome is an Italian.

clue.text: Horse without reins regularly runs and is a charm

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the horse's letters sit around the next piece

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is the nursery word for a horse

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word reins, starting with the first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse ridden without reins bolts, and that's lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', its older sense; 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'reins'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gris-gris is an African or voodoo amulet, a talisman worn for protection.

clue.text: Top decoration, award put on display

indicators.note: in an across answer, put on means placed after the preceding word

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An ornament for the top, an award shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a woolly ball used as an ornament on top of a hat.

clue.text: He painted collection boxes I in Germany, see

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the collection holds the German word

parts.note: a melange is a mixture or collection
ich is German for I
lo means look or see

explanation.surface: An artist decorated charity tins in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: MELANGE boxes ICH, then LO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance artist decorated the Sistine Chapel ceiling, so he is one who painted.

clue.text: This is learnt so a life can be better

definitions.text: This is learnt so a life can be better

indicators.note: the letters can be improved, that is reworked into a better order

explanation.surface: A self-help maxim: this lesson improves a life.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the fifteen letters of 'is learnt so a life'; the whole clue also describes the answer, with 'This' standing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulfilling one's own potential is something learnt over time that improves one's life.

clue.text: Child has confidence right away

parts.note: has, as in 'is sure', gives the verb is

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: to have confidence is to be sure

explanation.surface: A child is suddenly certain of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'has confidence' as 'is sure'; 'away' removes the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, as in 'died without issue'.

clue.text: Being dead cool, hiding gun

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-parrot, dead

indicators.note: the dead and cool pieces hide the gun inside them

parts.note: ice is cool, frozen water
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A dead cool character conceals a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead cool' reads as slang for very cool; split it, with 'dead' as ex- (former), and 'hiding' puts the gun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being and existence both mean the state of living or being real.

clue.text: She shares some riches out but not with male

indicators.note: out signals the letters are scattered and rearranged
the male letter is excluded from the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman hands out some of her wealth, but not to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SOE (SOME less M, by 'but not with') with RICHES. 'shares' looks like stock but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheiress is a woman who inherits jointly, so she shares an estate.

clue.text: This is pleasing if it's stuffed into certain envelopes?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the envelopes

parts.note: SAEs are stamped addressed envelopes

indicators.note: stuffed means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It's satisfying to stuff envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' scrambles 'if it's' to TISFI, and 'into' puts that inside the envelopes; 'certain envelopes' are the stamped addressed ones of British post.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy is to please, so the verb with 'this' as subject matches the phrase.

clue.text: Dancing like diva around home of viceroy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for home
dancing signals the letters of the phrase moving about

parts.note: H stands for house, a home

explanation.surface: A diva-like dancer circles a governor's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LIKE DIVA goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A khedive was the Ottoman viceroy of Egypt, and the adjective means relating to such a ruler.

clue.text: Sees differently, being about 50% colour blind

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the half colour
the letters of sees are arranged in a different order
half of the colour is lost

parts.note: yellow is a colour

explanation.surface: A partly colour-blind person sees things differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' scrambles 'Sees' to ESES, and 'about' wraps it round the first half of the colour (by '50%'); 'colour blind' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking eyes means being sightless.

clue.text: Praise officer after returning fire

indicators.note: the officer comes after the turned piece
returning means the word for fire is read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to axe them
LT is lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer praises the troops on their return from battle.
explanation.walkthrough: AXE reversed gives EXA, then LT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to glorify or extol.

clue.text: A trim little woman's packsaddle

parts.note: to pare is to trim
Jo March is one of the Little Women

explanation.surface: A neat little lady's saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo is a heroine of Louisa May Alcott's novel 'Little Women'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aparejo is a stuffed leather saddle for pack animals in Spanish America.

clue.text: Way teen's gone wild about lover stops nothing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the next piece
the letters have gone wild, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a fan is a lover of something
dams stop the flow of water

explanation.surface: A teenager runs riot over a boyfriend and blocks him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone wild' scrambles 'Way teen's' to SWEETNYA, 'about' wraps it round the lover after its fifth letter, and the stops follow. Sweet Fanny Adams is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase, euphemistic for a coarser one, means nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: Fire residue that keeps hot fire away

indicators.note: the residue keeps the letter for hot inside it

parts.note: soot is a residue of fire

explanation.surface: Soot retains heat, so the fire burns on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire residue' is SOOT; 'fire away' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Shoot!' means go ahead and speak, the same invitation as 'fire away'.

clue.text: Author first to show up

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, the British novelists

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of show

explanation.surface: A writer is the first to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the definition, as in 'something is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Something's up' and 'something's wrong' both mean all is not well.

clue.text: Old gas fire ultimately shared by two individuals

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fire

explanation.surface: An old gas fire was shared by a pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-one relationship or arrangement involves exactly two parties, each matched with the other.

clue.text: Earth initially smeared on some cricket balls

indicators.note: the letter is spread onto, and so into, the cricket matches

parts.note: Tests are international cricket matches, some of the game

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word Earth

explanation.surface: Dirt rubbed on cricket balls, as in ball-tampering.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; E goes inside TESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is slang for the male gonads, the anatomical term's everyday equivalent.

clue.text: Cast stop the show, none finishing as stars

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged
none of the three words keeps its finishing letter

explanation.surface: Actors stop the show, though none get to the end, as headliners.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the last letter of each word (P, E, W) leaves STOTHSHO, which 'Cast' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotshots are high-flying, brilliant people, the stars of their field.
